name: Trade war & tariffs
summary: Trump's 12 Nov threat to double tariffs on Mexican goods over a migrant caravan stands; no increase in force
state: On 12 Nov President Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexican goods, including steel, aluminium and vehicles, unless Mexico stops a migrant caravan from Chiapas (Mexico News Daily, 14 Nov). President Sheinbaum said caravans would not reach the US border (KJZZ, 12 Nov); no tariff increase or effective date had been set by 14 Nov. Sheinbaum is at APEC in Shenzhen on 17–19 Nov. Watch holds: a major tariff rise has been threatened but not imposed.
for_you: Higher US tariffs on Mexico would mainly affect car, steel and food supply chains; prices for imported goods tend to follow with a lag.
rubric_hit: Major tariff rise threatened between large economies = Watch

sources.title: Mexico News Daily — Week in review: Trump renews tariff threats
KJZZ — Sheinbaum says migrant caravans will not reach the border

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
